title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, October 2026 — the second regional Fed prices-paid read, published the same minute as the first
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/manufacturing-business-outlook-survey — the Philadelphia Fed's own MBOS landing page, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 277,628 bytes) by this event's own never-assessed initial research, independently of the empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15 sweep that first proposed the id. Its release-calendar block names the date and time verbatim: 'Oct 15 2026 October Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey 8:30 a.m.' CONFIRMED A SECOND WAY FROM THE SAME PRIMARY DOMAIN, and this is new: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events?release=manufacturing-business-outlook-survey (fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200, 131,089 bytes) embeds the FULL 2026 MBOS schedule as structured data — Jan 15 · Feb 19 · Mar 19 · Apr 16 · May 21 · Jun 18 · Jul 16 · Aug 20 · Sep 17 · Oct 15 · Nov 19 · Dec 17, every one at 8:30 a.m. All twelve are the third Thursday of their month, so the cadence rule and the enumerated calendar agree on every observation rather than on the two the landing page happens to show. October 2026's Thursdays are the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th, making the 15th the third. Filed estimate on the same two counts as its sibling empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15, neither of which is doubt about the date: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-08 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15.from-empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15.json, filed the same day by the Empire State lane) and then re-verified its primary independently — including the full-year calendar the proposal could not reach. That proposal is now inert and stays where it is. Impact LOW and symbols [] for reasons the ledger measures rather than assumes: the survey covers the Third District (Delaware, southern New Jersey, and eastern and central Pennsylvania — a sub-state footprint) via a qualitative diffusion survey of high-level executives, and its headline explains only 27% of the variance in national manufacturing industrial-production growth since 2001 (20% since 2015); no house playbook is keyed to regional surveys; none of the nine tracked names carries a Third District manufacturing channel; and on 2026-10-15 this print shares 8:30 ET with retail sales (high, confirmed) and PPI (medium, confirmed), so its own tape effect is unattributable by construction. What earns it a calendar row is the pair and the calendar arithmetic: 2026-10-15 is the ONLY morning in the visible 2026 schedule when Philly (third Thursday) and Empire (the 15th, rolled off weekends) publish in the same minute, and both surveys arrive at that morning in rare disagreement — the August headline gap is 26.8 points (Empire 20.6 vs Philly 47.4, the 97.4th percentile of 302 common months against a median of 8.4) and the prices-paid gap is 17.7 points (94.0th percentile against a median of 5.9). Philly's own August headline of 47.4 is the 99.0th percentile of 700 months back to May 1968. This is an ESTIMATE — it widens caution and licenses nothing; the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
